brief:
A Palestinian court has ruled that the Palestinian Authority must pay compensation to Israeli soldiers and police officers wounded in operations, the Ma'an news agency reported. The decision is the first of its kind to impose such financial liability on the Palestinian state for injuries sustained by Israeli security personnel.

The ruling establishes a new legal precedent in Palestinian courts. It remains unclear which specific incidents prompted the case, what amounts were awarded, or whether the Palestinian Authority plans to appeal the decision. The judgment reflects an unusual application of Palestinian law to require state compensation for Israeli military and police casualties from what the court apparently classified as actionable incidents rather than broader armed conflict.
title: Palestinian Authority ordered to compensate Israeli soldiers and police for attack injuries
